contract.enrichment: real 3D capture, CSS pointer tilt, and one 2.5D robot playing TWO scenes on a hatch cut into the header rail — football, then sitting down to write code
motionPrimitives: narrative mascot cycle, two scenes (rise · dribble · kick · turn · descend / rise · sit · type · close · descend)
performanceGuardrails: no WebGL or 3D runtime on homepage
no Lottie assistant payload on homepage
no requestAnimationFrame canvas for the About-like atmosphere
mascot cycle is 48s: ~16.6s scene one, ~24.5s scene two, ~6.9s fully below the rail and clipped out of paint
one rig for both scenes — no duplicated skeleton, no second set of animations running while hidden
sub-cycles all divide 48s exactly (0.3s key taps, 0.75s dust, 0.8s caret, 2.4s screen, 3s core) so they never drift
tilt disabled on touch and reduced-motion devices
transform and opacity only, plus discrete visibility used to switch paint off, never on
preservedFlows: all homepage href destinations except the explicitly requested authenticated Continue destination

iteration.brief: The mascot's face read straight at the viewer no matter which way it walked, and one scene was not enough. Redraw the head in three-quarter view so the turn actually turns the face; add a second scene where the robot climbs out with a laptop, sits on the rail and writes code.
variationKnobs: three-quarter head: nape block behind, visor pushed to the leading edge, far eye smaller than near eye
two scenes on one 48s timeline sharing a single rig
seated pose reusing the football leg rig (body drops 16, thigh -86°)
laptop with code lines that appear one at a time across two typing rounds
typing hands drawn into the laptop group so the lid cannot hide the key taps
six real statistics plus a counted-at provenance line
iteration.verifiedFrames: 30 paused samples across the 48s cycle in both themes, plus close-ups of the typing pose; rendered in headless Chromium by animation-delay sampling, and re-run against the production-built CSS rather than the source file
